notable_absence.finding: Slack's connection method is dual (Bot Token OR Webhook URL, with the note 'Connecting your integration with 1 Webhook URL allows you to send alerts to a single channel only. To send alerts to multiple channels, use a Bot Token'), unlike Microsoft Teams and Webhooks in this batch, which each support only a single Webhook-URL-based connection method. This is a real configuration-model divergence beyond payload format: Slack alone offers a second connection mechanism (Bot Token) with a materially different capability (multi-channel fan-out from one integration). Not minted as a cross-integration relation here since it would need a comparison concept (e.g. monitoring:microsoft-teams-alert-integration) this page alone doesn't establish - left for the reconciler to connect with configure-microsoft-integration.json and configure-webhook-integration.json's own extractions.

cross_component_finding: Confirms the batch hypothesis's 'shared shell, divergent detail' picture at the connection-method layer, not just the payload layer: the Prerequisites section (roles, Enterprise/Developer Pro Support Plan gate, static firewall IP allowlist of 3 addresses, up to 5 integrations per project) is verbatim-identical across this page, configure-microsoft-integration.md, and configure-webhook-integration.md, but Slack's own connection step adds a Bot Token option with distinct scopes (chat:write, channels:read, groups:read, optional chat:write.public) that neither Microsoft Teams nor Webhooks offers - a genuine per-tool capability difference, not just cosmetic payload-format variation.
